findings.issue: Participant clause (2) role-holder is ACTOR_ACTIVE-gated (verified: getRoleSlugsForActor applies ACTOR_ACTIVE_SQL to both primary+fallback employee lookup) and clause (3) owner is deactivation-safe, BUT clause (1) audit-actor match reads the append-only audit track and is NOT deactivation-gated. A user who was DEACTIVATED after having genuinely acted on the instance therefore still resolves as a participant during the residual ~300s access-JWT window (the T-0702/T-0726 window) and receives 200 skeleton + sourceRecord{title, canOpen:false}, whereas on current dev (T-0721) they would 404. Exposure is strictly bounded: canOpen is false (READ-PDP with their now-empty grants fails), no appId, NO variables/history/completedBy, NO record.data fields — the entire T-0721/T-0726 sensitive plane stays closed; only the record's human title label leaks, to someone who already legitimately acted on that instance, for ~5 min. Spec §1.2 acknowledges clause (1) is a past action (its reassurance 'denied the live record projection' is substantively true — canOpen:false, no openable record, no data — though the phrasing understates that a title-only projection IS returned).
findings.suggestion: Non-blocking. Consider a follow-up to either ACTOR_ACTIVE-gate the clause-(1) audit-actor set (align with clauses 2/3) or make the spec explicit that a deactivated former-actor retains title-only, canOpen:false skeleton visibility for the residual-JWT window. No sensitive-plane data is exposed, so this does not gate the merge.

findings.issue: When a projection is present with canOpen:false, projLinkAppId is null, but the initial targetAppId useState falls back to the legacy `appId` prop (projLinkAppId || appId || null). A caller passing BOTH a legacy appId prop AND a canOpen:false projection would momentarily render an <a> link on the first render before the useEffect (same tick) resets targetAppId to null. No actual call site does this (the two screen-process-instance call sites pass only recordId+projection+headers, appId undefined), and clicking the transient link hits GET /api/records/:id which is independently PDP-gated, so there is no security impact — a display-only edge for a hypothetical dual-prop caller.
findings.suggestion: Non-blocking. If desired, initialize targetAppId from projLinkAppId alone when hasProjection is true, ignoring the legacy appId prop, to avoid the one-frame link flash for a mixed-prop caller.
